pathway.title: CONSTELLIUM SE — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has fallen mainly because earnings rose, not because debt shrank (Documentary Fact from the financial base, with an Analyst Interpretation). Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag moved from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and total debt to the same measure from 2.70x to 1.71x. Earnings excluding lag rose by USD 345 million between those windows while total debt fell by USD 127 million. A ratio that falls on the numerator reverses if the earnings drivers reverse, so Constellium SE carries leverage that sits inside its 1.5x to 2.5x target range but has little demonstrated durability. Treating USD 417 million of receivables derecognized under factoring as debt-like lifts total debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag to 2.10x, an analyst sensitivity rather than a company measure.

Debt service is comfortable at current earnings (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag covered cash interest paid 10.65x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 6.92x for FY2025, and the senior notes carry fixed coupons, so rate moves do not change cash interest on the notes. The cover is earnings-dependent and shares the earnings quality caveat above.

Earnings quality is the central analytical issue (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Metal price lag was USD 222 million of USD 1,074 million of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported, 20.7%, and it turned negative at USD 4 million in Q3 2026 when aluminum prices fell. Revenue rose 26% in the nine months on higher revenue per ton while shipments were down 1%. In a rising price phase, inventories (USD 1,905 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 1,407 million at December 31, 2025) and receivables absorb cash, which is why nine-month 2026 working capital lines were an outflow of USD 488 million even as free cash flow of USD 223 million exceeded the USD 68 million of the prior-year nine months. Management attributes part of Q3 2026 to supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America; that is Management Language and cannot be assumed to persist.

Liquidity is adequate in the near term and the facility profile improved after quarter-end (Documentary Fact). Total liquidity of USD 992 million comprises USD 158 million of cash, USD 541 million of asset-based facility availability, USD 114 million of French facility availability and USD 179 million of factoring availability. Cash plus committed undrawn facilities is USD 813 million. The asset-based facility is undrawn and was amended on October 22, 2026 to raise commitments from USD 550 million to USD 700 million and extend maturity to October 22, 2031 (subsequent event; effect on availability not disclosed). The French facility, which matures in December 2027 per the annual report, is the nearest facility maturity.

The maturity wall is concentrated in 2029 and 2032 (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on refinancing cost). Face value of USD 225 million falls due in 2028, USD 841 million in 2029 (46.4% of USD 1,812 million total face value) and USD 691 million in 2032 (38.1%). The 2029 notes carry coupons of 3.750% and 3.125%, against 6.375% and 5.375% on the 2024 issues, so refinancing the 2029 notes at coupons like the 2024 issues would raise annual interest cost. The USD 100 million partial redemption of the 2028 notes in July 2026 shows a willingness to retire debt early when notes are callable at par.

Business risk rests on qualification-based relationships and is offset by concentration (Documentary Fact). Packaging and automotive rolled products supply 60% of revenue and 49% of segment earnings; the 10 largest customers are approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue; contracts in aerospace, packaging and automotive are mostly multi-year while general industrial contracts are one year or less. Metal cost is largely passed through, so margin risk sits in conversion margin, volumes and mix; the group has single-site loss precedent in the 2024 Valais flood.

Capital allocation is mixed (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on direction). Nine-month 2026 share repurchases of USD 78 million were alongside the partial note redemption; a new repurchase program of up to USD 300 million was authorized in March 2026 with about USD 257 million remaining, and no dividend is intended. Leverage inside the target range gives management room to continue returning cash, which competes with further debt reduction. Whether the indentures restrict that capacity cannot be tested.

Claims outside the debt figure add to the creditor burden (Documentary Fact). Pension and other benefit obligations were USD 341 million on the balance sheet at September 30, 2026, close-down and environmental provisions were USD 86 million, and the group is party to factoring programs under which USD 417 million of receivables were derecognized. None of these is in the USD 1,817 million of total debt.

cells.text: FY2025 revenue of 8,449 by segment before eliminations: Packaging & Automotive Rolled Products (P&ARP) 60%, Aerospace & Transportation (A&T) 23%, Automotive Structures & Industry (AS&I) 19%. Segment share of FY2025 Segment Adjusted EBITDA: P&ARP 49%, A&T 47%, AS&I 10%, Holdings & Corporate -6%.

Revenue and earnings are weighted differently: A&T is a smaller revenue block but nearly as large an earnings block as P&ARP, which points to higher conversion margins in aerospace (analyst interpretation). Loss of volume in P&ARP matters most for scale.
Products are priced on the LME price, a regional premium and a conversion margin; the model aims to pass metal cost through and hedge any remaining exposure.
Documentary Fact; the neutrality aim is Management Language
Metal price is largely a pass-through, so margin risk sits in conversion margin, volumes and mix; revenue and receivables scale with metal price.
Metal price lag is a non-cash timing effect between sales and purchase prices of metal and is included in Adjusted EBITDA as reported: 126 in FY2025 and 222 in 9M 2026, negative 4 in Q3 2026.

Earnings quality: part of reported Adjusted EBITDA is not cash; leverage should be read on the basis excluding lag (see CP-1: net 1.56x on that basis at September 30, 2026, 1.23x on Adjusted EBITDA as reported).
The average Midwest premium was 1,298 per ton in FY2025 against 432 in FY2024, and the all-in US aluminum price rose 38%.
US metal cost inflation raises working capital needs and inflates revenue; tariff policy remains an uncertainty the company itself flags.
The 10 largest customers represent approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue; relationships often span decades; qualification is rigorous and creates high switching costs.
Documentary Fact; the switching-cost description is Management Language
Concentration is material, offset by stickiness; a single large program loss or repricing would be visible in volumes.

Largest aerospace contracts are mostly multi-year; commercial transportation and defense are one to three years; general industrial one year or less; packaging and automotive contracts are typically multi-year, and automotive structures contracts usually last the life of a model.
Revenue visibility is strongest in aerospace, packaging and automotive programs and weakest in general industrial.

The top 10 metal suppliers are approximately 49% of metal purchases by volume; most slab and billet needs come from internal casthouses; energy is one of the largest operating costs after metal, labor and depreciation.
Supply concentration and energy cost are operating risks; internal casthouses reduce external dependency and support recycling margins.
Shipments were 1,120 thousand metric tons in 9M 2026 against 1,130 in 9M 2025 (down 1%); the 26% revenue rise in 9M 2026 came from higher revenue per ton, including metal prices.
Revenue growth is price-led, not volume-led, so revenue growth overstates operating growth.

Lowest volumes are typically delivered in August and December and highest from January to July; can demand is strongest in spring and summer and automotive and aerospace slow in the third and fourth quarters.
Quarterly cash flow is uneven; the third and fourth quarters are structurally weaker for volumes.

Cost of sales excluding depreciation and amortization was 86% of FY2025 revenue; the group employs approximately 11,500 people, about 50% of US employees and a majority of non-US employees under collective bargaining agreements.
Analyst interpretation: because metal is passed through, cost of sales moves with revenue, while labor under collective agreements is a less flexible cost.
Net capital expenditure was 311 in FY2025 and 197 in 9M 2026 (CP-1), described as relating primarily to maintenance and investments in manufacturing facilities.
Documentary Fact; the maintenance-and-investment description is Management Language
Capex runs near the level of depreciation (330 in FY2025), so free cash flow depends on holding spend discipline.
Inventories rose to 1,905 at September 30, 2026 from 1,407 at December 31, 2025 and receivables are partly sold under factoring (417 derecognized, CP-1).
Cash conversion depends on metal prices and continued factoring access.
FY2025 revenue by destination: United States 3,308, Germany 1,537, France 722, Spain 376, United Kingdom 367, Poland 317, Czech Republic 205, all other 1,617.
A large share of revenue is outside the US while reporting is in US dollars; foreign exchange is hedged for commercial exposures.

Management attributes Q3 2026 results to an improved aerospace and transportation, industry and defense environment, supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America and strong recycling performance.
Part of the earnings uplift rests on market conditions management itself calls shortages; they may not persist.

runs.text: Strengths. Customer relationships protected by qualification (Documentary Fact): switching costs and mostly multi-year contracts in the largest end markets support volume visibility and retention. Leverage and coverage (Documentary Fact): net leverage of 1.56x and cash interest cover of 10.65x leave debt service comfortable at current earnings, and a cushion against a moderate earnings decline. Liquidity and maturity runway (Documentary Fact): USD 992 million of total liquidity, an undrawn asset-based facility with a longer tenor after the October 2026 amendment, and no senior notes maturing before 2028 give time to manage a downturn. Fixed-rate funding (Documentary Fact): fixed coupons on the senior notes limit cash interest sensitivity to rates. Diversified end markets and footprint (Documentary Fact): three segments across aerospace, packaging and automotive and 23 manufacturing facilities spread the operating base across regions.

Weaknesses. Earnings quality (Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation): a fifth of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA as reported is non-cash metal price lag, and revenue is price-led. Cash conversion sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation): working capital absorbs cash when metal prices rise and the group relies on factoring. Concentration (Documentary Fact): 10 customers are approximately 56% of revenue and the largest segment is 60% of revenue. Refinancing (Analyst Interpretation): the 2029 maturities are 46.4% of face value and carry coupons below those of the 2024 issues. Capital allocation (Analyst Interpretation): repurchases compete with deleveraging while leverage sits near the low end of the target range. Unknown creditor protections (Insufficient Information): covenant levels, guarantors, indenture baskets, ownership and ratings are not available, so recovery mechanics, structural subordination and distribution capacity cannot be assessed.

runs.text: The context supplies no transaction: deal terms, sponsor, borrower and parent are blank, so there is no transaction to analyze and no sponsor behavior to assess. The record of capital structure events in the supplied sources is as follows. In August 2024 the company issued dollar and euro senior notes due 2032 and, with cash on hand, redeemed the remaining 2026 dollar and euro notes, which left no senior notes maturing before 2028 (completed; 10-K page:65, 109). In July 2026 it redeemed part of the 5.625% notes due 2028, leaving a smaller outstanding amount (completed within Q3 2026; 10-Q Q3 page:15). No new debt issue occurred in Q3 2026 in the pages read, and the debt table shows no new instrument. On October 22, 2026, after the quarter-end and within the cutoff, the US asset-based facility was amended to raise commitments and extend maturity (a subsequent event, described in CP-1; 10-Q Q3 page:23); the 10-Q lists the amending agreement as Amendment No. 8 filed as Exhibit 10.1 (10-Q Q3 page:43), so the document exists but is not in the pack, and its terms beyond commitment size and maturity are Not supplied. This refines the earlier readiness note, which described the amendment document as not supplied; that remains true of the pack. On shareholder returns, a new repurchase program of up to 300 was authorized on March 12, 2026, effective May 21, 2026 and expiring December 31, 2028, replacing the previous program; about 257 remained at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:43). The board approved cancellation of 6 million treasury shares on September 17, 2026, with no cash effect (10-Q Q3 page:13). A 54% interest in Changchun Engley Automobile Parts Co. LTD was disposed of on June 24, 2026 for net cash of 2 (10-Q Q3 page:23). In Q3 2026 the group also settled the Ravenswood Salaried Pension Plan through lump-sum payments and an annuity purchase, derecognizing 47 of obligations and 44 of assets (10-Q Q3 page:20). Credit effect: these actions reduce interest-bearing debt modestly and the amendment raises facility commitments, but they leave the 2029 and 2032 maturities unchanged (see CP-1); the use of cash for repurchases competes with further debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is solid and fully sourced from filed statements for FY2025 and for the nine months to September 30, 2026, with the quarter taken from the filed statements and the release. On the group's own leverage definition, which divides net debt by last-twelve-months Segment Adjusted EBITDA that excludes non-cash metal price lag, leverage moved from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x at September 30, 2026 by our calculation, close to the 1.6x the company reports. The improvement came mostly from earnings, not from deleveraging: total debt fell by 127 while earnings excluding metal price lag rose by 345 between FY2025 and the LTM to September 30, 2026. On Adjusted EBITDA as reported, which includes metal price lag, the same ratios are lower (1.23x net at September 30, 2026), so the basis chosen matters and is shown. Cash interest cover, liquidity and the maturity profile are comfortable in the near term, with the main structural facts being fixed-rate unsecured notes that mature mainly in 2029 and 2032, a secured asset-based revolver that is undrawn, and sizable off-balance-sheet receivables factoring. The view is limited because covenant levels, the credit agreement and the indentures are not in the pack, and because Adjusted EBITDA and net debt are management measures.

fields.value: Risk mechanic: the improvement is mostly numerator-driven. Earnings excluding lag rose by 345 between the FY2025 and LTM windows (720 to 1,065) while net debt fell by 165 (1,824 to 1,659). A leverage ratio that falls on earnings is exposed to a reversal in the earnings drivers: the company attributes the quarter to improved aerospace and transportation conditions, supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America and strong recycling, and the P&ARP segment rose 98% in Q3 on favorable metal costs and price and mix (10-Q Q3 page:24, 36). Treating the factoring programs as debt-like lifts the ratio: total debt plus the 417 derecognized receivables over LTM earnings excluding lag is 2.10x (calculated; not a company or covenant measure).

fields.name: Quote

Cash interest cover of 10.65x is comfortable. Covenant headroom cannot be assessed because levels are not supplied.

The lag turned negative in Q3 2026 (-4), which the company ties to primary aluminum prices decreasing (Release Q3 page:6). Metal price lag was 21% of 9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported (222 of 1,074, calculated), so in a rising price phase reported Adjusted EBITDA runs ahead of cash earnings.

Pan-U.S. ABL availability of 541 against commitments of 550 is far above the 10% trigger for the fixed charge coverage test (55 on the 550 of commitments, calculated), so on the face of the figures the test would not be required; the borrowing availability definition is not supplied, so this is indicative only. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The senior note indentures carry incurrence-style limits on debt, restricted payments, liens, asset sales and mergers, and a 101% change-of-control offer (10-K page:35, 108). The only maintenance covenant located is the fixed charge coverage ratio on the Pan-U.S. ABL, tested only if availability falls below 10% of commitments. The company states compliance with all applicable financial debt covenants at March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026 (each quarterly debt note) and at December 31, 2025 and 2024 (10-K page:110). The covenant level, the definition and the reported ratio are Not supplied. Definition differences that matter: Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation, factoring expenses, restructuring, impairment, unrealized derivative gains and losses and non-operating pension items, and includes metal price lag; the company's leverage uses Segment Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes lag; net debt as defined by the company adjusts for cross-currency basis swaps net of margin calls and for cash pledged for guarantees (Release Q3 page:12); and factoring expense (15 in 9M 2026) sits in other gains and losses, outside finance costs. The metric computed here (carrying-value debt less cash over EBITDA excluding lag) differs from the company's only by the 1 swap adjustment at September 30, 2026.

fields.value: Constellium SE is the French parent of a global converter of aluminum into rolled and extruded products for aerospace, packaging and automotive customers, organized in three segments. Risk mechanic: qualification and switching costs support retention and volume visibility, but concentration means a loss or repricing at one account moves volumes and margin materially; general industrial contracts are one year or less. Credit implication: revenue visibility supports debt service in the near term, while a downturn in packaging or automotive volumes would weaken coverage; the concentration risk factor is stated by the company (10-K page:30). Credit implication: an operational disruption at a key rolling site (the 2024 Valais flood is an example of site-level loss) can affect a large share of earnings; insurance proceeds offset part of that loss (10-K page:68, 61).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Constellium SE has a sound fundamental credit profile, with moderate and falling leverage, adequate liquidity and no senior notes maturing before 2028. Net debt was USD 1,659 million, or 1.56x Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag, at September 30, 2026, against 2.53x at FY2025, and total liquidity was USD 992 million. The strongest support is qualification-protected, mostly multi-year customer relationships in aerospace, packaging and automotive. The weakest point is earnings quality: 20.7% of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported was non-cash metal price lag, and management links part of the uplift to supply shortages. What decides the outcome is whether margins hold as metal prices and those shortages normalize, and how the USD 841 million of 2029 notes is refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen mainly because earnings rose, not because debt shrank (Documentary Fact from the financial base, with an Analyst Interpretation). Net debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding metal price lag moved from 2.53x at FY2025 to 1.56x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, and total debt to the same measure from 2.70x to 1.71x. Earnings excluding lag rose by USD 345 million between those windows while total debt fell by USD 127 million. A ratio that falls on the numerator reverses if the earnings drivers reverse, so Constellium SE carries leverage that sits inside its 1.5x to 2.5x target range but has little demonstrated durability. Treating USD 417 million of receivables derecognized under factoring as debt-like lifts total debt to Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag to 2.10x, an analyst sensitivity rather than a company measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service is comfortable at current earnings (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA excluding lag covered cash interest paid 10.65x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 6.92x for FY2025, and the senior notes carry fixed coupons, so rate moves do not change cash interest on the notes. The cover is earnings-dependent and shares the earnings quality caveat above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the central analytical issue (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Metal price lag was USD 222 million of USD 1,074 million of nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA as reported, 20.7%, and it turned negative at USD 4 million in Q3 2026 when aluminum prices fell. Revenue rose 26% in the nine months on higher revenue per ton while shipments were down 1%. In a rising price phase, inventories (USD 1,905 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 1,407 million at December 31, 2025) and receivables absorb cash, which is why nine-month 2026 working capital lines were an outflow of USD 488 million even as free cash flow of USD 223 million exceeded the USD 68 million of the prior-year nine months. Management attributes part of Q3 2026 to supply shortages of automotive rolled products in North America; that is Management Language and cannot be assumed to persist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate in the near term and the facility profile improved after quarter-end (Documentary Fact). Total liquidity of USD 992 million comprises USD 158 million of cash, USD 541 million of asset-based facility availability, USD 114 million of French facility availability and USD 179 million of factoring availability. Cash plus committed undrawn facilities is USD 813 million. The asset-based facility is undrawn and was amended on October 22, 2026 to raise commitments from USD 550 million to USD 700 million and extend maturity to October 22, 2031 (subsequent event; effect on availability not disclosed). The French facility, which matures in December 2027 per the annual report, is the nearest facility maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The maturity wall is concentrated in 2029 and 2032 (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on refinancing cost). Face value of USD 225 million falls due in 2028, USD 841 million in 2029 (46.4% of USD 1,812 million total face value) and USD 691 million in 2032 (38.1%). The 2029 notes carry coupons of 3.750% and 3.125%, against 6.375% and 5.375% on the 2024 issues, so refinancing the 2029 notes at coupons like the 2024 issues would raise annual interest cost. The USD 100 million partial redemption of the 2028 notes in July 2026 shows a willingness to retire debt early when notes are callable at par.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk rests on qualification-based relationships and is offset by concentration (Documentary Fact). Packaging and automotive rolled products supply 60% of revenue and 49% of segment earnings; the 10 largest customers are approximately 56% of FY2025 revenue; contracts in aerospace, packaging and automotive are mostly multi-year while general industrial contracts are one year or less. Metal cost is largely passed through, so margin risk sits in conversion margin, volumes and mix; the group has single-site loss precedent in the 2024 Valais flood.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation is mixed (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on direction). Nine-month 2026 share repurchases of USD 78 million were alongside the partial note redemption; a new repurchase program of up to USD 300 million was authorized in March 2026 with about USD 257 million remaining, and no dividend is intended. Leverage inside the target range gives management room to continue returning cash, which competes with further debt reduction. Whether the indentures restrict that capacity cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure add to the creditor burden (Documentary Fact). Pension and other benefit obligations were USD 341 million on the balance sheet at September 30, 2026, close-down and environmental provisions were USD 86 million, and the group is party to factoring programs under which USD 417 million of receivables were derecognized. None of these is in the USD 1,817 million of total debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Customer relationships protected by qualification (Documentary Fact): switching costs and mostly multi-year contracts in the largest end markets support volume visibility and retention. Leverage and coverage (Documentary Fact): net leverage of 1.56x and cash interest cover of 10.65x leave debt service comfortable at current earnings, and a cushion against a moderate earnings decline. Liquidity and maturity runway (Documentary Fact): USD 992 million of total liquidity, an undrawn asset-based facility with a longer tenor after the October 2026 amendment, and no senior notes maturing before 2028 give time to manage a downturn. Fixed-rate funding (Documentary Fact): fixed coupons on the senior notes limit cash interest sensitivity to rates. Diversified end markets and footprint (Documentary Fact): three segments across aerospace, packaging and automotive and 23 manufacturing facilities spread the operating base across regions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Earnings quality (Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation): a fifth of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA as reported is non-cash metal price lag, and revenue is price-led. Cash conversion sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation): working capital absorbs cash when metal prices rise and the group relies on factoring. Concentration (Documentary Fact): 10 customers are approximately 56% of revenue and the largest segment is 60% of revenue. Refinancing (Analyst Interpretation): the 2029 maturities are 46.4% of face value and carry coupons below those of the 2024 issues. Capital allocation (Analyst Interpretation): repurchases compete with deleveraging while leverage sits near the low end of the target range. Unknown creditor protections (Insufficient Information): covenant levels, guarantors, indenture baskets, ownership and ratings are not available, so recovery mechanics, structural subordination and distribution capacity cannot be assessed.
